values.note: Reservations by phone (417) 995-2050 or email; no online booking. Two-night minimum on every nightly stay, three on holiday weekends. Groups over 4 people pay $6 a day per extra person (children 6 and under free).

booking.source: https://eveningstarcamping.com/rates.html ('For Reservations call: 417-995-2050'; '$40.00 per night with 2 night minimum'; '$50.00 per night holiday weekends with 3 night minimum'; 'Groups larger than 4 people are subject to a surcharge of $6.00 per day for each additional person') + https://eveningstarcamping.com/ ('For reservations call (417) 995-2050 or email us'), read 2026-11-06

note: Mostly seasonal: the operator leads with monthly and yearly pad rentals and weekend packages ('We rent our RV sites monthly or yearly'), and RVs can be left on their pads over the winter; nightly stays are also sold. About 2 miles east of Stockton Lake's Mutton Creek Public Use Area; small catch-and-release fishing pond, boat storage. --Claude
summary: Operator pages re-read: confirmed 42 full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, showers and laundry, $40 nightly (2-night minimum, $50 holiday weekends with 3), booked by phone/email (platform phone). Note cleaned (MINIMUM STAY line is now booking.min_stay) and now says the park is mostly seasonal. The fishing ponds are well under an acre; not waterfront stands.
flags: Long-stay tests (monthly, weekend-package, full-time and yearly pads marketed; 'We rent our RV sites monthly or yearly'): (1) price $40 nightly, $50 holiday weekends - passes; no gateway (Branson 110 km), family has not stayed; (2) nightly rate on its own site + phone (417) 995-2050 - passes; (3) minimum 2 nights on every stay, 3 on holiday weekends - passes (not over 2 outside holidays); (4) no count of nightly vs seasonal sites anywhere - passes by default, but Esri imagery (leaf-off winter frame) shows the main loop nearly full of RVs, consistent with 'At the end of the camping season, you may leave your RV on your pad for $70.00 per month'; (5) RV park, no homes or lots for sale - passes. I read it as mostly seasonal but passing; not 'iffy': Google 4.4 from 34 reviews.

Ratings: Google 4.4 / 34 ('Evening Star Campground, Stockton Lake, MO', phone (417) 995-2050); RV Life 5 stars from 1 review, $ tier. Recent negative Google reviews: 'No grass, no picnic tables but the worst thing was the fireworks! ... The fireworks were set off by the "manager" and went on for over an hour. Also no WiFi.' (Julie, edited 4 months ago); 'if you like lots of ticks ... owner doesn't want to put spray down' (Big Hillbilly, edited a year ago).
Rate date: the rates page carries no year (footer '©2020 Evening Star Camping'), so the $40/$50 figures are the operator's current page but cannot be dated 2024+ from the page itself.

Pin 37.5396,-93.7539 sits by the entrance road ~200 m north of the main RV loop (Google's pin 37.5377,-93.7531 is on the loop); a centroid of the pads is about 37.5380,-93.7533 - under the 250 m line, optional move.
Waterfront: the 'stocked pond for catch and release' and its neighbour are each well under an acre on Esri imagery (~45 x 30 m); Stockton Lake is ~2 miles away. Not waterfront stands.
